subject: SXSW 2026 Lead Flow Audit & Post-Event Credits
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@omnicloud.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@omnicloud.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick question on SXSW lead attributions and promised credits

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the booth and the session — we appreciated the traffic and the demo. A couple of our RevOps folks flagged that 48 leads we expected to be marked as 'SXSW' in our CRM are showing as organic or unknown. We thought there was an agreement to credit all booth-scan leads and demo signups that were captured at the event.

Can you confirm: 1) which attribution rule you used to tag leads as SXSW, and 2) whether Redwood will honor the previously discussed marketing credit for leads that lost the SXSW tag due to mapping/UTM issues? Jordan is on this thread and can share their export if helpful.

Appreciate a quick flag — they want this in the renewal workbook.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Field & Events
OmniCloud

--
Marta R.
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@omnicloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on SXSW lead attributions and promised credits

Hi Marta — thanks for flagging this. Short answer: we used an attribution rule that prefers form-source (booth-scan form) first, then session-utm, then last-touch. That should have captured booth-scan and demo signups, but I agree 48 sounds like an outlier.

Ben / Dylan — looping you in to double-check the exports and the credit calculation. Ben, please confirm the HubSpot filter used and whether any known ingestion issues occurred between Mar 11–14. Dylan, can you pull the booth-scan CSV from our event tablet backups (I think you still have them) and the session signup list?

Marta — we'll aim to turn around a reconciled list and a proposed credit within 72 hours. If we find the mismatch is on our side (UTM mapping or import drop), Redwood will apply the agreed per-lead credit to the Nov invoice. If it's due to changes on OmniCloud's side (e.g., form renames), we'll document findings and propose next steps.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0184

--
Evelyn Hart
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-03T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on SXSW lead attributions and promised credits

Evelyn / Dylan,

I pulled the HubSpot export for the SXSW campaign (filter: campaign = "SXSW2026" OR utm_campaign contains "sxsw"). Initial notes:
- HubSpot shows 1,032 leads attributed to SXSW.
- There are 48 leads with source = (none) or organic that matched booth-scan emails in OmniCloud's export Jordan shared earlier.
- Ingestion log shows a short Spike in API errors on 2026-03-13 02:14–02:47 UTC — some batch imports retried and eventually landed, but three small batches timed out and were dropped. That correlates with ~38 of the 48 missing tags.

I attached sxsw26_lead_export.csv and a short doc explaining the attribution rules. The key issue is the import-timeouts: booth-scan rows that failed to re-ingest lost the campaign value (HubSpot set source=manual import). Those rows exist in our backup CSV but HubSpot lost the utm_campaign field on import.

Recommendation: reconcile the backup CSV against HubSpot and re-import the missing campaign value as a one-off patch (we can do this with minimal risk). On credits: per our contract appendix, per-lead credit is $120 for booth-qualified leads. If we patch HubSpot to restore the campaign tag for those 48 and confirm they meet qualification criteria, Redwood will apply the agreed credit on the Nov invoice.

Attachments: sxsw26_lead_export.csv, attribution_rules_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

--
Ben C.
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on SXSW lead attributions and promised credits

Folks — I pulled the booth tablet export and cross-checked against Ben's HubSpot export. Notes from the retro and data check: 
- Booth tablet backup contains 1,128 scan records. After dedup and quality checks (email verification, role filter), 1,010 unique leads qualified as booth contacts.
- Matching logic (email exact match) found 962 matches in HubSpot, 48 unmatched as Ben flagged.
- Of the 48 unmatched, 10 have intentional opt-outs or bounced emails (we shouldn't credit these). The remaining 38 look like clean matches but the utm_campaign was stripped during the failed import.

I built a quick credit calc and put it in sxsw_credit_calc.xlsx. Proposal: patch the 38 clean matches to set campaign = "SXSW2026" in HubSpot, validate qualification fields (role, company size), and apply credit for 38 leads at $120 = $4,560. Exclude the 10 bounced/opt-outs.

Operational ask: Ben, can your team run the one-off patch on the 38 rows and add a note to each record: "post-event credit applied — import error 2026-03-13"? Evelyn, if you approve I'll schedule the patch for Nov 6th 02:00–03:00 PST (low traffic).

Retro: we should consider a fallback process so future booth-scan batches hit our S3 intermediate storage with checksum and retries to avoid HubSpot API timeouts.

Dylan
Event Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

--
Dylan B.
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@omnicloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on SXSW lead attributions and promised credits

Hi Marta — thanks for your patience. Quick summary and next steps: 

Summary of findings
- Root cause: transient HubSpot import timeouts on 2026-03-13 caused a small set of booth-scan rows to lose the utm_campaign value. Those rows show up in our backup CSV but were imported with source = manual import.
- Count for credit: 38 booth-qualified leads (10 additional rows excluded for bounce/opt-out).
- Credit calculation: 38 * $120 = $4,560 (will be applied as a line-item credit on your Nov invoice under Contract DEAL-8743).

Actions we will take (timeline)
- Nov 07 (today): Ben will patch the 38 HubSpot records to set campaign = "SXSW2026" and append a CRM note describing the patch (Ben: please include the import error code/time).
- Nov 08: Dylan will rerun the QA and confirm the records meet qualification criteria; he will upload the reconciliation workbook to the shared Drive link.
- Nov 10: Redwood Finance will post the $4,560 credit on the Nov invoice; I'll confirm once posted.

Operational follow-up (retro items)
- Implement S3 intermediate staging for booth-scans + checksums to prevent direct HubSpot timeouts.
- Add a monitoring alert for import failures that hits on >1% batch loss.

If OmniCloud is OK with that plan, we'll proceed and close the ticket. Thanks again for raising this — sorry for the noise in your renewal pack.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0184

Attachments: sxsw_credit_calc.xlsx

--
Evelyn H.
